selected.title: Assistant treasurer knew about ATO's credit card ban plans months ago
selected.summary: Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino concedes the government knew the Australian Taxation Office was considering banning credit card payments in July, months before the decision was made public.

( ABC News: Ian Cutmore ) In short: The assistant treasurer says the government knew in July the tax office was considering a credit card ban following the Reserve Bank's surcharge changes. Outrage about the change from the business community forced the prime minister to step in. What's next? The issue has exposed tensions between the prime minister and the treasurer. abc.net.au/news/federal-politics-insiders-daniel-mulino-ato-credit-card-ban/107280382 Link copied Share Share article Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino has conceded the government knew the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) was considering banning credit card payments in July, months before the decision was made public. The ATO's decision in late September to stop accepting credit card payments from December 1 sparked backlash from the business community. That outrage eventually forced an intervention from the prime minister and the treasurer to underwrite the costs and allow credit cards to be accepted by the tax office until mid-2027. Mr Mulino today said he and Treasurer Jim Chalmers were first made aware of the ATO's intentions months ago. "In July, the government became aware that the ATO was looking at options and that at that point their preference was to not accept credit cards," Mr Mulino told ABC's Insiders. "The indication we gave to the ATO was that they should continue to engage with the credit card companies, and that there should be a transition period." The admission comes after the Australian Financial Review yesterday revealed the ATO had privately informed the government about its credit card ban and presented the government with options.
